page: UpCloud PREMIUM-38xCPU-192GB is a compute- and memory-balanced virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by the AMD EPYC 9575F processor featuring an x86_64 architecture, providing 38 vCPUs corresponding to 38 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 192.0 GB of system memory, which allocates approximately 5.05 GB per core. For local storage, the instance comes bundled with a 500 GB SSD. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete hardware GPUs are attached to this plan.

Benchmark results place the AMD EPYC 9575F compute performance at a high level. Single-core execution scores within the top tier, reflected in a stress-ng score of 3952.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2568.0. Multi-core performance remains competitive, registering a Geekbench multi-core result of 23049.0, a stress-ng multi-core metric of 100700.89, and a PassMark CPU score of 71873.69. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, facilitating strong results in tasks such as Clang compilation (50005.0) and ray tracing (61334.0).

Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read throughput of 250.52 GB/sec and uncached write throughput of 107.36 GB/sec on 256MB blocks, alongside cached small-block reads of 7289.98 GB/sec. Despite raw throughput, the aggregate PassMark memory score settles into the middle tier at 1857.46. Application benchmarks highlight top-tier database operations in PassMark (34302.15) and solid throughput in Redis SET operations (64.19 million operations/sec). CPU-based LLM inference achieves 2858.81 tokens/sec prompt processing on a 135M model, but drops to 12.7 tokens/sec for generation on a 7B model, reflecting the absence of hardware accelerators.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of physical cores, substantial RAM, and integrated 500 GB local SSD storage on a shared-CPU allocation model. This resource profile fits workloads demanding parallel execution and significant memory footprints without requiring dedicated GPU hardware, such as relational databases, in-memory caching layers, Clang software build farms, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-38xCPU-192GB is a high-capacity virtual instance offering 38 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 192.0 GB of memory (5.05 GB per core), and a bundled 500 GB SSD on a KVM hypervisor. Running x86_64 architecture with full AVX-512 support, the system demonstrates top-tier single-core and strong multi-core compute metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench. Large block memory read throughput reaches 250.52 GB/sec, supporting strong in-memory and data-processing tasks such as Redis caching (64.19M ops/sec) and PassMark database operations (34302.15). While CPU-only architecture limits larger LLM generation speeds, the server provides balanced compute density and ample memory capacity. It serves as an effective platform for compiled software pipelines, large-scale database backends, static web delivery, and data processing workloads.
